summary: Cloud-scale simulation and evaluation infrastructure for physical AI systems.
editor_note: Thousands of repeatable scenarios turn simulation into a continuous verifier, not a final demo environment. Teams connect their own hardware, sensors, software and models, then inspect failures and feed real-world results back into calibration. The practical edge is the workflow: local Isaac Sim or Isaac Lab authoring, cloud execution and regression analysis around one physical system. Customer results are company and investor statements, not VentureDex-reproduced benchmarks.

product_evidence.claim: The product site exposes local Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab authoring, cloud dispatch across repeatable scenarios, CI/CD integration, failure analysis, digital-twin calibration and an agent-assisted workflow.
Antioch says its platform integrates customer hardware, sensors, software, models and constraints, then runs cloud-scale evaluations and uses real-world outcomes to recalibrate the simulator.
Greylock says it led the Series A and describes high-fidelity simulations calibrated to customer hardware, thousands of parallel evaluations and a named customer relationship with Amazon Ring.

market_context.primary_user: Engineering teams building robots, drones, autonomous vehicles, intelligent perception and automated manufacturing systems.
market_context.category: Physical AI simulation and evaluation infrastructure
market_context.differentiation: A continuously calibrated environment that joins customer-specific hardware and software with cloud-scale scenario evaluation and regression analysis.
market_context.why_now: Physical systems are improving faster than physical test programs can cheaply reproduce rare failures, hardware changes and deployment conditions.

risks.claim: The published accuracy and development-speed benefits come from company, investor and customer statements; VentureDex did not independently reproduce them.
risks.basis: Source-bound VentureDex assessment of Antioch and Greylock announcements.
